newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia betting shops seen in price squeeze.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia betting shops seen in price squeeze.

text.p: More than half of Tabcorp Holdings Ltd's commissioned betting agencies in the state of Victoria might close over the next year if the company is unable to avoid a 164 percent price increase for the Sky Channel service, an agents' association official said on Friday.

"It we don't pay it (the annual fee hike), half the network at least closes, if we do pay it half the network closes. We're in a no-win situation," senior vice president of the Victorian TAB Agents' Association Evelyn Bakken told Reuters.

Sky, owned equally by businessman Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd and Rupert Murdoch's News Corp Ltd, has demanded the fee hike for the channel in order for Tabcorp to renew its contract which ran out in June this year, Tabcorp said in a letter to agents this week.
"The heavy handed position adoped by Sky will likely accelerate the closure of agencies to a much greater degree than ever contemplated by Tabcorp or agents," the company said.

But Sky, which holds a virtual monopoly on direct television broadcasts of greyhound, thoroughbred and harness racing in Australia, said it would not budge on the fee hike as it was necessary to recoup the cost of broadcasting rights in Victoria.

"We're standing by that increase because it equates to the money it costs us to pay for that product from Victoria. My board is resolute in its decision to stand by its...fee increase," Sky managing director Bill North told Reuters.
Tabcorp, which operates in Victoria only, said that under the lapsed contract it paid annual fees of A$3 million for Sky.
Half of those fees were then charged to agencies on a sliding scale pegged to turnover figures.
TAB's Bakken said the Sky service was vital for attracting punters but many small agencies would not be able to absorb the fee increase.
"(Agencies) will cease to exist without the Sky channel picture," she said.
Tabcorp spokeswoman Jill Hollingworth told Reuters that negotiations with Sky were continuing but would not comment on the possible impact on revenues if the agency network was rationalised heavily.
In the year to June 30, 1996 Tabcorp's net profit was A$63.4 million on turnover of A$557 million, 48 percent of which came from TAB agencies.
At 0250 GMT (12.50 p.m.) Tabcorp shares were up 11 cents to A$6.32.
